nodes.label: FellowshipAnalyzer Architecture Overview
nodes.rationale: Kept concise and factual as the current implementation reference; procedural workflows deliberately live in skills rather than being appended here.

nodes.label: Per-Report Analysis Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Fixed ordering (deserialize, normalize, construct modules, dispatch) guarantees analyzers only ever see hydrated, scaled, correctly ordered events, so no analyzer has to defend against raw-log irregularities.

nodes.label: Combat Event Model
nodes.rationale: Events are mutable classes rather than structs so normalizers can hydrate, link, and annotate them in place; capability interfaces (IAbilityEvent, IHasSourceEvent, IHasTargetEvent) let subscription filters work structurally instead of per-concrete-type.

nodes.label: Parser Source Generation
nodes.rationale: Attributes on the parser are compiled into constructors, typed accessors, type lists, and DI registration, keeping hero parsers small and declarative and keeping registration reflection-free for AOT WebAssembly builds.

nodes.label: Module Lifecycle
nodes.rationale: There is deliberately no Initialize/Complete virtual: setup runs in the constructor and metrics are computed on read or from a FightEndEvent handler, which removes an entire lifecycle phase that could be forgotten or ordered wrongly. Modules must not take CombatLogParser in their constructor because the parser assigns Owner only after DI resolution.

nodes.label: Two-Tiered Module Activation
nodes.rationale: The mutable Active flag handles dynamic deactivation that must respect mid-fight state, while [ActiveWhen<TPredicate>] gates at parser-construction time from ParseContext (including SelectedCombatant) so inapplicable modules are never constructed at all.

nodes.label: Pull-Lifetime Analyzer
nodes.rationale: A fresh Analyzer instance per matching pull makes per-pull state correct by construction rather than by manual reset; instances are retained on pull read surfaces so guides can read them after analysis. Analyzers may depend on [AddState] fight-lifetime modules but never on other analyzers (FA0014).

nodes.label: Analyzer Surface Read Paths
nodes.rationale: The surface type is the topmost ancestor deriving directly from Analyzer (or the IAnalyzerSurface marker), so shape-specialized subclasses with disjoint [ForPull] filters collapse into one cross-pull stream that a guide can read without knowing the shape split.

nodes.label: Declarative Event Subscription
nodes.rationale: [On<TEvent>] attributes with By/To/Spell/ExtraSpell arguments are compiled by ModuleGenerator into RegisterSubscriptions plumbing with inlined predicates, so filtering costs nothing at runtime and subscriptions cannot drift from the handler they belong to.

nodes.label: Normalizer Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Execution follows the generated normalizer type list (declaration order, base normalizers before hero normalizers); Priority is retained and kept aligned because implementations and comments use it as documentation of intended order.

nodes.label: Fabricated Fight Bookend Events
nodes.rationale: FightBookendNormalizer prepends FightStartEvent and appends FightEndEvent so every module gets a guaranteed first and last dispatch to hook setup and finalization, without a separate lifecycle callback.

nodes.label: Resource Tracking
nodes.rationale: One base tracker observes every ResourceTypes the selected player exhibits and keys ResourceState per type; hero subclasses only supply what the log cannot provide (cost lookup via GetResourceCost, caps via MaxOverrides).

nodes.label: Hero Project Layout
nodes.rationale: Every hero mirrors the Rime layout (Modules/Guides/Statistics/Normalizers) so folder position alone identifies a file's role; shared spell identity lives in Core while gameplay metadata lives in the hero Abilities module.

nodes.label: UI Integration
nodes.rationale: The parser's GuideComponent points at the hero root guide, which manually composes feature guides; statistics are auto-collected from active modules exposing a non-null StatisticsComponentType, so adding a card needs no central registry edit.

nodes.label: Generated Hero DI Registration
nodes.rationale: AddCoreAnalysis() must be registered before Add{Hero}Analysis() so shared analysis services, base modules, and base normalizers exist before hero registrations layer on keyed IHeroAnalyzer entries.

nodes.label: JSON-To-C# Event Schema Mapping Procedure
nodes.rationale: Type discriminators resolve either via [FSLEventDiscriminator] or by stripping the Event suffix and lowercasing; naming is then reconciled through CamelCase policy, case-insensitive matching, [JsonPropertyName], and [JsonIgnore] before any mismatch is called a bug.

nodes.label: Deserialization Mismatch Severities
nodes.rationale: Silent data loss (unmapped JSON property, non-nullable C# property for an optional JSON field, type conflict, nested-vs-flat mismatch) is High severity; a C# property with no JSON counterpart is Low because normalizers legitimately fabricate synthetic fields.

nodes.label: No Hand-Maintained Event Schema
nodes.rationale: A static schema document would drift from the logs; the tool is rerun against the relevant log every time rather than relying on remembered snapshots.

nodes.label: Inferred-Versus-Confirmed Resource Meaning
nodes.rationale: Resource semantics deduced from observed change patterns must be labelled as inference rather than confirmed source behaviour, and a missing sourceResources.resources structure is reported as absent instead of guessed at.

nodes.label: Pull-Lifetime Versus Fight-Lifetime Split
nodes.rationale: Pull-lifetime Analyzer with [ForPull] is the default for gameplay analysis because per-pull state comes free; fight-lifetime EventSubscriber registered with [AddModule] or [AddState] is reserved for cross-pull state, statistics sources, and infrastructure.

nodes.label: Get-Style Metric Exposure
nodes.rationale: An analyzer finalizes nothing at pull end: its state is frozen once listeners clear, so a getter always sees final state. Intervals still open at pull end read Pull.EndTime inside the getter; heavy multi-output computations memoize behind a private nullable field. [On<PullEndEvent>] is reserved for the one thing getters cannot do - snapshotting a fight-lifetime module's live state at the instant the pull closes.

nodes.label: Analyzer Composition Patterns
nodes.rationale: Three patterns cover pull-shape variation: one flat analyzer matching every shape; independent analyzers sharing an IAnalyzerSurface marker interface when they answer different questions and share no behaviour; an abstract base with shape-specialized subclasses when they share subscriptions and state and differ only in finalization. Inheritance is earned only when the base owns real machinery - a base implementing every strategy while subclasses one-line-dispatch wants the flat pattern instead.

nodes.label: Lazy<T> Cross-Module Injection
nodes.rationale: Lazy<T> defers resolution to dispatch time so mutually referencing modules can ctor-inject without tripping the FA0013 cycle diagnostic; ModuleGenerator emits a cached _camelCaseName accessor for every Lazy<TModule> primary-ctor parameter. Plain non-Lazy injection remains fine for acyclic dependencies.

nodes.label: Typed-Data-Only Module Boundary
nodes.rationale: Modules hold counts, rates, timestamps, enums, and typed entry records only. Prose, severity wording, and PerformanceTier judgments live in the consuming Razor component, keeping analyzers pure C# with no Razor, RenderFragment, or Blazor dependency.

nodes.label: Analyzer Roslyn Diagnostics (FA0013/FA0014/FA0016/FA0017)
nodes.rationale: FA0013 flags module dependency cycles (Lazy<> edges exempt), FA0014 forbids analyzer-to-analyzer dependencies, FA0016 enforces disjoint [ForPull] filters across analyzers sharing a surface, FA0017 limits an analyzer to at most one surface interface.

nodes.label: Fabricated Pull Bookend Events
nodes.rationale: PullBookendNormalizer fabricates a start/end pair around each pull and the parser re-emits PullEndEvent to that pull's own analyzers exactly once as it closes, including on a force-close.

nodes.label: Guide Component Pattern
nodes.rationale: A guide injects the hero parser and reads analyzer instances directly rather than through an intermediate report model; it owns all presentation (prose, severity wording, PerformanceTier judgments) and keeps display-shaping helpers in its @code block.

nodes.label: ToPullRows / ToItemRows Row Projection
nodes.rationale: The row builder returns a PerCastRow carrying only varying fields while the extension fills pull-derived grouping (FormatTimestamp label, Group name, PullBanner), so guides never hand-build PerCastData. PerformanceTiers.FromThresholds replaces hand-written tier ladders.

nodes.label: Merging Analyzers Across Pull Shapes In A Guide
nodes.rationale: A shared surface marker interface lets a guide read one stream and switch on the concrete analyzer type per row; overview stats partition the same stream with OfType<>. Sections are gated on the single stream being non-empty rather than on per-shape checks.
nodes.norm_label: merging analyzers across pull shapes in a guide

nodes.label: Shared Guide UI Widget Set
nodes.rationale: GuideSection, CastOverview, CastDetail, GradiatedPerformanceBar, PassFailBar, PerformanceBoxRow, SpellSequence, StackedBar, and StatCard live in FellowshipAnalyzer.Core.UI.Guides and are preferred over bespoke markup.

nodes.label: Auto-Collected Statistics Component
nodes.rationale: A statistics component inherits AnalyzerStatistic<T> and receives its module through a CascadingParameter instead of injecting the parser, so the framework can collect every active module with a non-null StatisticsComponentType and render it via DynamicComponent with no central registry. Statistics stay summary-focused; per-cast detail belongs in guides.

nodes.label: ResourceTracker Subclass Pattern
nodes.rationale: A hero subclass is justified only by convenience accessors, MaxOverrides, spell-definition cost lookup, or a statistics component. MaxOverrides is set in the constructor because Module.Initialize no longer exists, and the class must be partial so ModuleGenerator can emit the inherited [On<>] subscriptions. The tracker registers before analyzers that depend on it since declaration order is module priority.

nodes.label: ResourceTypes Enum Discipline
nodes.rationale: Analyzer code uses ResourceTypes rather than raw resource IDs, and a real log is inspected before a new enum value is added so the enum stays derived from observed data instead of guessed.

nodes.label: IEventNormalizer Implementation Pattern
nodes.rationale: Normalizers are explicitly not modules: no Module base, no Initialize/Complete, no event subscriptions. They are registered with [AddNormalizer<T>] rather than [AddModule<T>], resolved from DI so they can ctor-inject services, and must return a complete event list.

nodes.label: Reordering, Linking, And Fabrication Techniques
nodes.rationale: Linking uses a (Timestamp, SourceId, Ability.FSLID) lookup to attach LinkedEvent references; fabrication emits synthetic events marked Fabricated with a Trigger back-reference. Mutating the input list is allowed when intentional, but returning a new list is clearer for reordering and filtering.

nodes.label: Hero Project Scaffold
nodes.rationale: A hero is a Razor Class Library referencing Core, Components, and Generators (as an Analyzer with ReferenceOutputAssembly=false). No constructor is written and Analyze is never overridden - the source generator and base CombatLogParser supply the pipeline. The hero must also be added to the HeroName enum, given a Hero static field with its HeroRole, and included in Hero.All.

nodes.label: Hero Spell Registry In Core
nodes.rationale: Spell identity (id, name, icon) lives in Core under Common/Spells/{Hero}/ so it is shared, while gameplay metadata such as cooldowns, GCD, categories, and costs belongs in the hero Abilities module or spell init properties rather than being embedded in analyzer logic.

nodes.label: Hero Abilities Module
nodes.rationale: The hero Abilities module overrides Spellbook() with SpellbookAbility entries; the source generator registers it as a scoped service and aliases it to the core Abilities type so core normalizers can inject it without knowing the hero.

nodes.label: File-Based dotnet Tool Convention
nodes.rationale: Tools are single .cs file-based apps with no .csproj, declaring dependencies via #:package directives, and are always run from the repository root so relative paths resolve.

nodes.label: FellowshipLogs Tool Credentials
nodes.rationale: API tools read a user-secrets store id from a non-committed .env file (USER_SECRET_ID), and the keyed store holds FellowshipLogs:ClientId and FellowshipLogs:ClientSecret, keeping credentials out of the repo.

nodes.label: fetch-abilities Tool
nodes.rationale: Writes abilities.json at the repo root and exits immediately if the cached file exists; --refresh forces a re-fetch after a game patch adds abilities.

nodes.label: event-schema Tool
nodes.rationale: Prints every unique event type with all properties, frequency, and JSON value kinds; accepts a raw report at data.reportData.report.events.data, a top-level array, or any nested array of event objects.

nodes.label: refresh-schema Tool
nodes.rationale: Converts docs/schema.json introspection output to SDL at Api.GraphQL/schema.graphql; --no-fetch skips the network call. A rebuild afterwards retriggers StrawberryShake's source generator.

nodes.label: resource-analysis Tool
nodes.rationale: Prints a Markdown summary of unique resource types across sourceResources.resources, with amount/max ranges, change patterns, and common event/ability pairings.

nodes.label: update-spells Tool
nodes.rationale: JSON is authoritative for name and icon; the tool matches by numeric id and only updates existing entries, never adds new ones. Spell versus Effect/Talent/Weapon is decided by the C# declaration on each line, and combat-log guids map by FSLID million-ranges (effects >= 1,000,000, talents >= 2,000,000, weapon traits >= 3,000,000).

nodes.label: SCSS File Conventions
nodes.rationale: .razor.scss is always the source of truth and .razor.css is generated output that a build will overwrite, so a compiled .razor.css is never edited and never authored. AspNetCore.SassCompiler handles compilation with no manual step, and partials (_tokens, _mixins) are only ever @used.

nodes.label: Design Token System
nodes.rationale: _tokens.scss is the only file permitted to contain a colour literal; everything else references a token. SCSS function arguments take t.$fa-* while plain property values take var(--fa-*) so runtime overrides and DevTools edits survive. Custom properties need #{} interpolation because Sass does not evaluate --* values and would emit the token name as literal text.

nodes.label: One-Token-Per-Colour Tint Scale
nodes.rationale: Transparency comes only from the fixed tint scale via tint(), never from rgba() or an alpha-suffixed token, because a palette with twenty near-identical whites cannot be designed with. An off-scale tint is drift, not a requirement - snap to the nearest step. A genuinely new colour adds one base token, never a variant of an existing one.

nodes.label: Scoped Versus Global Styling
nodes.rationale: Scoped .razor.scss is the default because Blazor's scope attribute removes collision risk; app.scss is reserved for layout primitives, resets, typography, and genuinely universal utilities. :global() and ::deep are avoided except for third-party overrides.

nodes.label: Shallow SCSS Nesting
nodes.rationale: Nesting is capped at three levels because deeper trees make the resulting selector unreadable; & is used for pseudo-classes and state modifiers, while element parts are written as explicit flat sibling classes.

nodes.label: Hero-Specific Accent Tokens
nodes.rationale: Each hero declares its own accent locally (Rime uses --fa-ice); hero-specific tokens must never leak into shared FellowshipAnalyzer.Components styles.

nodes.label: Common SCSS Pitfalls
nodes.rationale: Recurring failures: editing compiled output, creating .razor.css, hardcoded hex, rgb()/rgba() outside _tokens.scss, inventing colour variants, off-scale tints, uninterpolated tokens in custom properties, inline style for static presentation, and pushing single-component rules into app.scss. Inline style is legitimate only for dynamic values computed in C#, such as performance bar widths.

nodes.label: Atomic Design With Flat Hyphenated Class Names
nodes.rationale: Atomic level (atom/molecule/organism) guides how to name but is never a class prefix. Names stay lowercase and hyphenated with BEM's __ and -- banned outright, because Blazor scoping already prevents collisions so BEM's disambiguation buys nothing. State is expressed as a compound class alongside the root rather than a modifier suffix.
nodes.norm_label: atomic design with flat hyphenated class names

nodes.label: Performance Tier Modifier Classes
nodes.rationale: The .perfect/.good/.ok/.fail classes map one-to-one onto the C# PerformanceTier enum and the --fa-perf-* tokens, and are always applied as modifiers alongside a base class. @include mx.perf-tier-colors emits all four at once so the mapping is defined in exactly one place.

nodes.label: Size Modifier Naming
nodes.rationale: Size variants use sm/md/lg suffixes applied alongside the component root class rather than separate component names.

nodes.label: Card / Panel Surface Pattern
nodes.rationale: A bordered inset surface built from mx.card-surface (bg-card, gold border, radius-md, shadow-card) with flat -header/-title/-body parts; used for statistics, data sections, and standalone info blocks.

nodes.label: Guide Section Two-Column Layout
nodes.rationale: Explanation text left, data panel right, with the split controlled by an --explanation-pct CSS variable passed from Razor via inline style so the ratio is a per-usage decision rather than a new class; collapses to one column at the mobile breakpoint.

nodes.label: Performance Box Row Pattern
nodes.rationale: Small coloured squares representing per-cast performance, wrapping in a flex row; .clickable adds hover affordance and mx.perf-tier-colors supplies the four tier colours.

nodes.label: Spell Badge Filmstrip Pattern
nodes.rationale: Inline wrapping badges whose border colour is set from C# via inline style (a legitimate dynamic-value use) while size variants badge-sm/md/lg stay in SCSS.

nodes.label: Timeline Row With Sticky Label
nodes.rationale: Horizontal scrolling content with a fixed-width position:sticky left label column that inherits its background from the parent so the sticky area does not show content sliding beneath it.

nodes.label: Responsive Stats Grid
nodes.rationale: Three equal columns collapsing to one at the mobile-sm breakpoint via mx.mobile-sm.

nodes.label: Eyebrow Label Global Utility
nodes.rationale: A small all-caps section label defined once in app.scss as a genuinely universal utility and explicitly never redefined in a component.

nodes.label: Server-Side Persistent Cache Architecture
nodes.rationale: A persistent cache layer sits behind the existing IMemoryCache in Api.Core, exposed through one DI-injected interface so the source-generated endpoint adapters and FellowshipLogsApiHandler stay implementation-agnostic. All three tiers use Azure Blob Storage uniformly; Cosmos DB was dropped because per-document TTL is not worth a second SDK, a second cost line, and a second emulator.

nodes.label: IPersistentCache Abstraction
nodes.rationale: Partition-plus-key and stream-oriented (GetAsync/SetAsync/SetStreamAsync/RemoveAsync) specifically to avoid buffering large event payloads. It lives in Api.Core but is registered by each host rather than by AddFellowshipLogsApi, so DevApi and the Functions app can bind different backing stores.

nodes.label: BlobPersistentCache
nodes.rationale: Shared by both hosts and depending only on a host-registered BlobServiceClient. Containers are created lazily once per partition behind an AsyncLazy<> so startup does not pay for containers a request never touches. Production credentials use Managed Identity via DefaultAzureCredential, with no connection strings in app settings.

nodes.label: CachePartition Tiering
nodes.rationale: GameData, Metadata, and Events map one-to-one onto blob containers, letting each get its own storage tier for cost: gamedata Hot (rarely changes, hit often), metadata Hot (small, hot), events Cool (large, and single-user rereads are dominated by the client IndexedDB cache).

nodes.label: L1/L2/L3 Cache Layering
nodes.rationale: L1 IMemoryCache stays in-process for analysis and character but is skipped entirely for events because those payloads are too large to retain in process; L2 is the persistent cache; L3 is the upstream FellowshipLogs call, which writes back through the layers using the existing FellowshipLogsCacheOptions durations rather than a new TTL model.

nodes.label: Blob Metadata TTL Strategy
nodes.rationale: Per-blob expiresAt metadata with lazy expiration on read (return null and fire-and-forget delete) plus container lifecycle policies for bulk cleanup - deliberately no background job, which is what made dropping Cosmos affordable.

nodes.label: Streaming Gzip Events Path
nodes.rationale: RecyclableMemoryStream avoids a fresh byte[] per request and lets the reshaped JSON be teed to both the HTTP response and the blob writer without double-buffering. Gzip is preserved end to end (ContentEncoding on the blob, Content-Encoding on the response) so the server never decompresses what the browser will decompress anyway. Events are only cached when the fight is not InProgress.

nodes.label: Aspire Azurite Emulator Orchestration
nodes.rationale: DevApi runs the real BlobPersistentCache against an Azurite emulator orchestrated by Aspire for full production parity; a NullPersistentCache and a filesystem cache were both rejected because they would not exercise the real code path in development.

nodes.label: Client IndexedDB Report Cache
nodes.rationale: IndexedDbReportCacheService already covers the per-user browser story for events and master data, so the only client change is honouring a new X-FellowshipAnalyzer-ExpiresAt response header on the IndexedDB read path. No Blazored.LocalStorage or Dexie dependency is added - the existing JS module plus IJSRuntime is kept, consistent with WASM download-size discipline.

nodes.label: FellowshipAnalyzer (project overview)
nodes.rationale: Combat log analysis tool for the online RPG Fellowship: reads Fellowship Logs reports, runs hero-specific analyzers over combat events, renders guide and statistics views.

nodes.label: Hero Project Boundary
nodes.rationale: Hero projects are intentionally pre-created and separate as a contributor-experience choice as much as an architecture choice: a contributor should be able to open one hero's project, add a module, and stay inside that boundary. Cross-hero sharing goes through Core or Components, never a direct hero-to-hero project reference.

nodes.label: Download Size Discipline
nodes.rationale: Release builds are Blazor WebAssembly with AOT, so every dependency in client, core, components, or hero projects is downloaded by the browser and AOT-compiled. Initial download size is therefore a first-class constraint; the per-hero project boundary is kept as a future-friendly point for lazy loading.

nodes.label: Source Generation And Registration
nodes.rationale: Hero analyzers are registered without runtime reflection because the client is Blazor WebAssembly with AOT; the parser source generator reads [HeroAnalyzer] and [AddModule<T>] attributes and emits typed constructors, module accessors, DI registration, and keyed IHeroAnalyzer registration.

nodes.label: AddFellowshipHeroAnalysis (aggregate registration)
nodes.rationale: Single reflection-free aggregate registration method called by the WebAssembly client alongside AddCoreAnalysisServices() and AddCoreAnalysis(); each new hero adds its generated Add{Hero}Analysis() call here explicitly.

nodes.label: Layered Directory.Packages.props
nodes.rationale: Root file enables central package management; src/ owns source versions, src/Heroes/ is reserved for hero-only browser-side packages, tests/ owns test versions. Project files use versionless PackageReference entries.

nodes.label: Working On A Hero Analyzer
nodes.rationale: Canonical per-hero folder layout ({Hero}CombatLogParser.cs, Modules/, Guides/, Statistics/, Normalizers/) and the five-step contribution sequence: abilities metadata, module, [AddModule<T>] registration, guide/statistics component, hero tests.

nodes.label: Aspire App Host Local Orchestration
nodes.rationale: The app host wires the Blazor host and Azure Functions API together; default app URL http://fellowshipanalyzer.dev.localhost:5120 and API on http://localhost:5123. Requires Docker and Azure Functions Core Tools v4.

nodes.label: Per-Report Per-Hero Analysis Pipeline
nodes.rationale: FellowshipLogs API JSON -> polymorphic event deserialization -> CombatLogParser.Analyze -> IEventNormalizer pass -> Module.Initialize (Events.* fluent filters) -> EventEmitter dispatch -> Module.Complete -> HeroAnalysisResult -> Razor guide/statistics components.

nodes.label: Hero Parser Pattern
nodes.rationale: Parsers are small and declarative: [HeroAnalyzer], [AddState<T>], [AddAnalyzer<T>], [AddModule<T>] attributes on a partial class; the generator emits the constructor, typed module properties, GetModuleTypes(), GetNormalizerTypes(), and an Add{Hero}Analysis() DI extension.

nodes.label: Module Lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Modules are scoped DI services. Owner and Priority are assigned by the parser after DI resolution, so modules must not accept CombatLogParser in their constructors. Subscribe in Initialize(), accumulate during dispatch, finalize in Complete(), expose read-only state to UI; reach other modules via Owner.GetModule<T>() or generated parser properties.

nodes.label: Reflection-Free Hero Registration
nodes.rationale: Roslyn source generators register hero analyzers reflection-free specifically for AOT compatibility; runtime reflection must never be introduced for analyzer discovery.

nodes.label: Size Discipline (Blazor WASM + AOT)
nodes.rationale: Before adding a PackageReference, ask whether it must run in the browser; server-only deps belong in API/host projects. Prefer framework APIs and small helpers over utility libraries.

nodes.label: No Cross-Hero Project References
nodes.rationale: Shared behavior between two heroes must be lifted into Core or Components rather than creating a project reference between hero projects, preserving the per-hero boundary and lazy-loading potential.

nodes.label: Comment Policy
nodes.rationale: Comments are reserved exclusively for API/usage notes: never reference design docs or plan.md points, and never add inline or in-method comments.

nodes.label: WoWAnalyzer Port-Priority Audit
nodes.rationale: Owner-reviewed 0-10 port priorities for every WoWAnalyzer shared module, parser UI, and guide component, with verified already-have equivalents, shippable feature bundles, and a dependency-ordered build roadmap. Consulted when planning shared-infrastructure or hero-analyzer work.

nodes.label: RimeCombatLogParser (reference parser)
nodes.rationale: Rime is the most complete hero reference implementation; its parser demonstrates [AddState<WinterOrbTracker>], [AddAnalyzer<SingleTargetRimeCombo>], [AddAnalyzer<AoERimeCombo>], and GuideComponent => typeof(RimeGuide).

nodes.label: Shipped Hero Projects
nodes.rationale: Aeona, Ardeos, Elarion, Helena, Mara, Meiko, Rime, Sylvie, Tariq, Vigour, Xavian - one Razor class library per hero under src/Heroes/.

nodes.label: Solution Layout
nodes.rationale: Core (events/parser/spell data), Core.Contracts (API-client DTOs), Generators (Roslyn source generators), Analyzers (Roslyn diagnostic analyzers, distinct from gameplay analyzers), Components (Razor + SCSS), Heroes, Api/DevApi/DevHost, Tools.

nodes.label: Contribution Workflow
nodes.rationale: Most gameplay contributions should stay inside one hero project; prefer small focused changes. Local setup needs .NET 10 SDK with the WASM workload, Azure Functions Core Tools v4, and Docker; Fellowship Logs credentials go on the DevApi project because Aspire does not forward AppHost user secrets to children.

nodes.label: Pull Request Checklist
nodes.rationale: Solution builds; new analyzer behavior has focused tests; hero code stays in its hero project; shared abstractions justified by more than one use; package versions in the nearest Directory.Packages.props; browser-facing deps size-conscious; missing data surfaced as loading/error state rather than placeholder IDs or fallback labels.

nodes.label: Choosing Where Code Goes
nodes.rationale: Hero-specific logic in the hero project; shared events/parser/filters/base analyzers/spell data in Core; reusable Razor UI in Components; Fellowship Logs access in FellowshipLogs or Api; generator changes in Generators. No direct hero-to-hero references.

nodes.label: Source Generation Rules
nodes.rationale: Analyzer discovery and DI registration are source-generated and reflection-free because the client runs as Blazor WebAssembly with AOT; use the existing attributes instead of runtime scanning and keep Add{Hero}Analysis() registration explicit.

nodes.label: Package And Dependency Rules
nodes.rationale: No Version attributes on individual PackageReference entries. Blazor WebAssembly AOT makes dependency size expensive, so prefer framework APIs, small helpers, server-only deps in server projects, and shared components only when reuse is real.

nodes.label: UI And Styling Rules
nodes.rationale: Reusable display pieces in Components, hero-specific guide/statistics in the hero project. Use .razor.scss alongside the component, reuse component design tokens, keep guide/statistics UI data-driven from analyzer state, avoid large media assets.

nodes.label: Module Lifecycle Expectations
nodes.rationale: Subscribe in Initialize(), track state during dispatch, compute summaries in Complete(), expose read-only state for UI, and use Owner.GetModule<T>() or generated parser properties for module dependencies.

nodes.label: Hero Analyzer Contributions
nodes.rationale: A normal analyzer change touches Modules/Abilities.cs metadata, a module inheriting Analyzer/ResourceTracker/Auras, an [AddModule<T>] entry on the hero parser, a guide or statistics component, and hero tests.

nodes.label: Fellowship Combat Mechanics for Log Analysis
nodes.rationale: Fellowship uses a WoW-style rating system with tiered diminishing returns and a unified Haste stat; these mechanics can be modeled deterministically by combining published rating-to-percentage formulas with empirically verified haste scaling on cooldowns and GCD.
nodes.norm_label: fellowship combat mechanics for log analysis

nodes.label: Secondary Stats and Rating System
nodes.rationale: Four gear secondaries - Critical Strike, Haste, Expertise, Spirit - stored as ratings. Ratings come from gear/gems/effects; talents, set bonuses, and gem effects add flat percentages that stack after the rating-to-percentage and DR steps.

nodes.label: Rating to Percentage Conversion
nodes.rationale: All secondaries share a base conversion of 0.017 percentage points per 1 rating before DR (100 rating = 1.7%). The analyzer partitions rating into DR tiers, multiplies each tier by its effective factor, sums, adds non-diminished flat bonuses, adds crit base 5%, and rounds to 2 decimals.

nodes.label: Tiered Diminishing Returns on Secondary Stats
nodes.rationale: Piecewise P(R): 0-589 at 0.017, 589-898 at 0.01615, 898-1242 at 0.014535, 1242-1647 at 0.01235475, >1647 at 0.009901. Intent is to make low stats feel strong early and discourage extreme single-stat stacking; flat percentage bonuses bypass DR entirely.
nodes.norm_label: tiered diminishing returns on secondary stats

nodes.label: Critical Strike 5% Base (DR-exempt)
nodes.rationale: Crit computation is post-DR percentage from rating plus a 5% base explicitly exempt from diminishing returns, plus any flat crit bonuses from gems, talents, or set bonuses.

nodes.label: Haste-Adjusted Time Scaling
nodes.rationale: T_effective = T_base * 100 / (100 + H_total), applied uniformly to GCD, cast time, tick interval, and haste-scaling cooldowns. 100% haste halves duration; 50% haste yields a one-third reduction (H / (H + 100)).

nodes.label: Global Cooldown Modeling
nodes.rationale: Base GCD is treated as a configurable per-hero parameter defaulting to 1.5s because official docs are absent and reports conflict on a 1.0s baseline; the model is validated against empirical minimum inter-cast intervals in real logs.

nodes.label: Ability-Specific Cooldown Recovery Modifiers
nodes.rationale: Compute the generic haste-adjusted cooldown first, then apply ability recovery: C_effective = C_haste * 100 / (100 + R_ability). Flat reductions such as 'reduce cooldown by 1.5s on crit' are event-driven reductions on the remaining cooldown at proc time.

nodes.label: Chronoshift (800% increased cooldown recovery)
nodes.rationale: Extreme recovery effect: multiplier becomes 100 / 900 ~= 0.111, so an already haste-reduced cooldown drops to about one-ninth of its haste-only value during the channel.

nodes.label: Tick Timing for Periodic Effects
nodes.rationale: DoTs/HoTs tick at base interval * 100 / (100 + H_total). Practical approach: model each periodic effect as a tick schedule from first application timestamp plus haste snapshot, then align actual log ticks against the schedule to detect downtime and clipping.

nodes.label: Haste Snapshots vs Dynamic Updates
nodes.rationale: Snapshot rules are not publicly documented, so the analyzer assumes cooldowns and GCD are determined at cast start from current H_total, treats tick intervals as snapshotted at application time, and exposes configuration flags for snapshot vs dynamic behavior pending more data.

nodes.label: Core State to Track Per Player
nodes.rationale: Secondary ratings, derived post-DR percentages, active haste/cooldown-recovery buffs and debuffs, per-ability cooldown state, GCD lock state, and resource state (mana, hero-specific resources, Spirit) - updated at each log event to simulate what the player could have done versus what they did.
nodes.norm_label: core state to track per player

nodes.label: Reconstructing Ability Cooldowns
nodes.rationale: On each cast: compute H_total(t), compute C_effective, set next-available to t + C_effective, then apply proc-driven reductions as they appear. Comparing predicted ready timestamps to actual casts yields wasted cooldown time and drift metrics.

nodes.label: Metrics Enabled By These Mechanics
nodes.rationale: Cooldown alignment, drift and desync, GCD utilization, stat utilization relative to the 10-25% efficient band, and haste-adjusted buff/debuff uptime - surfaced per-pull and per-ability to give feedback beyond raw DPS/HPS.

nodes.label: Archon Fellowship Logs
nodes.rationale: Archon's Fellowship Logs parses the game's combat log file into damage breakdowns, buff uptime, and death reasons, confirming the log carries enough structured data to serve as ground truth for event sequencing.

nodes.label: WoWAnalyzer (upstream project)
nodes.rationale: FellowshipAnalyzer is essentially a C#/Blazor WebAssembly clone of WoWAnalyzer adapted for Fellowship: analysis patterns, module structures, guide and statistics concepts, the normalizer pipeline, and the event-driven design all derive from it, ported from TypeScript/React and adapted for source generators and compile-time analyzer registration.

nodes.label: AGPL-3.0 License Lineage
nodes.rationale: FellowshipAnalyzer is distributed under AGPL-3.0 in recognition of its lineage from WoWAnalyzer, which uses the same license; contributions are accepted on those terms.

nodes.label: White Gold Palette
nodes.rationale: Five-step warm ramp #FFFAF1, #EDDDB8, #DCC080, #CAA347, #B8860E.

nodes.label: Blue / Grey Steel Palette
nodes.rationale: Six-step cool ramp #7AB3D0, #3383B1, #2A4677, #989A9F, #B3B6BB, #CDCDCC.

nodes.label: Angry's S2 Elarion Guide
nodes.rationale: The Rotation and Advanced Topics sections of this guide are the research input from which every proposed Elarion analyzer module is derived.

nodes.label: Lunarlight Mark Eruption Analyzer
nodes.rationale: Top AoE priority is erupting Lunarlight Marks with Heartseeker Barrage or Impending Heartseeker; the common mistake is casting Barrage/Impending with no marks on targets, wasting the eruption mechanic. Higher crit can burn marks prematurely with other abilities.

nodes.label: Empowered Multishot Waste Analyzer
nodes.rationale: AoE priority 5 is 'don't waste empowered Multishot charges'. Empowered Multishot must always be cast before a regular Multishot; casting the regular version while empowered charges are available is a clear-cut rotation mistake, making this the highest-priority module to build.

nodes.label: Highwind Arrow Cap Analyzer
nodes.rationale: AoE priority 6 is 'don't overcap Highwind Arrow charges'. With 3 charges, sitting at max wastes recharge time; tracked as time at 3/3, casts made while already capped, and charge-seconds wasted.

nodes.label: Cooldown Efficiency Analyzer (Skystrider's Grace + Event Horizon)
nodes.rationale: Use these on cooldown only when the full durational value is obtainable; holding is a DPS loss but wasting them on short windows is also bad. Tracks casts, held-time past cooldown, and effective vs maximum buff duration. Chosen fourth because the pattern is reusable across multiple cooldowns.
nodes.norm_label: cooldown efficiency analyzer (skystrider's grace + event horizon)

nodes.label: Pre-Ultimate Checklist Analyzer
nodes.rationale: Scores each Spirit of Heroism window against the pre-ult sequence (Skystrider's Supremacy -> Voidbringer's Touch -> Skystrider's Grace + Event Horizon) plus Barrage/Impending availability. High value but needs correlation across multiple buff and cast events.

nodes.label: Starfall Volley Desync Analyzer
nodes.rationale: AoE priority 3 desyncs Lunarlight Mark and Starfall Volley by 10-15s; casting them together wastes the window where marks could be reapplied and erupted between Volley casts. Flags Volley within 5s of a Mark cast.

nodes.label: Impending Heartseeker Proc Tracking
nodes.rationale: Focused Shot triggers Impending Heartseeker procs (bad-luck protection). Procs stack twice, last 15s, and a second proc resets the first timer; letting procs expire unused is waste.

nodes.label: Voidbringer's Touch Usage Analyzer
nodes.rationale: Send the first cast ASAP then save for void -> ults -> void, and never double-mark the same target before the first mark is consumed; misuse wastes spirit generation from Visions of Grandeur. Ranked last because it needs target tracking plus spirit resource correlation.

nodes.label: ElarionAuras (existing module)
nodes.rationale: One of only three existing Elarion modules; supplies the buff tracking the Pre-Ultimate Checklist needs to identify Spirit of Heroism windows.

nodes.label: FocusTracker (existing module)
nodes.rationale: Existing Elarion resource tracker; the current minimal Elarion guide shows only its Focus resource graph.

nodes.label: Elarion Implementation Order
nodes.rationale: Ordered by impact over complexity: simple, clear-cut waste detectors first (Empowered Multishot, Highwind Arrow), then core rotation mechanics, then reusable cooldown patterns, then multi-event correlation work. Dependencies include existing Elarion spell IDs in Spells.cs, event normalizers to link mark applications to targets, and buff tracking from ElarionAuras.

nodes.label: CI Build Solution Job
nodes.rationale: Runs on ubuntu-latest with submodules checked out, .NET 10.0.x, restore and Release build of FellowshipAnalyzer.slnx. Triggered on pull_request to master with cancel-in-progress concurrency.

nodes.label: CI Test Matrix (Core, Generators, Heroes.Rime, SpellData)
nodes.rationale: fail-fast disabled; four test projects run independently with trx loggers and uploaded artifacts. Only Rime among the eleven heroes has a CI-gated test project.
nodes.norm_label: ci test matrix (core, generators, heroes.rime, spelldata)

nodes.label: RunAOTCompilation=false in CI
nodes.rationale: AOT is disabled on every restore, build, and test invocation so PR validation does not pay the WebAssembly AOT compilation cost; AOT is exercised only on the deploy path.

nodes.label: Azure Static Web Apps Build and Deploy Job
nodes.rationale: Push to master publishes the standalone Blazor WebAssembly client and the Functions API separately, then uploads both via Azure/static-web-apps-deploy with OIDC id-token auth and skip_app_build/skip_api_build.
nodes.norm_label: azure static web apps build and deploy job

nodes.label: wasm-tools Workload Cache
nodes.rationale: Caches ~/.dotnet sdk-manifests, packs, metadata, and library-packs keyed on the resolved SDK version so the expensive wasm-tools workload install is skipped on cache hit.

nodes.label: Static + API Split Deploy Layout
nodes.rationale: app_location publish/static/wwwroot serves the prerendered WASM client bundle, api_location publish/api hosts the Functions API as SWA managed functions on the same hostname.

nodes.label: Serena Project Configuration
nodes.rationale: Registers FellowshipAnalyzer with the Serena code-intelligence agent: csharp language server only, utf-8 encoding, gitignore-driven file exclusion, read/write enabled, no excluded tools.

nodes.label: S3 'Rise of the Heskyr' Data Dump
nodes.rationale: Season 3 went live 2026-06-22 with a full progression reset, new hero Gunde, Loot 2.0, a stat squish, and new zones. The repo was restructured season-first as /s2/<resource>.json and /s3/<resource>.json.
nodes.norm_label: s3 'rise of the heskyr' data dump

nodes.label: Health and Damage Scaling Formulas
nodes.rationale: Health and damage follow the same shape: ROUND(ROUND(base * Multiplier) * DifficultyScaleMultiplier). The S3 stat squish moved base main stat 1700 -> 120 and base health 28560 -> 2856, sourced from the CT_CharacterBaseAttributes Default row.

nodes.label: S3 vs S2 Diminishing Returns Tiers
nodes.rationale: S3 softened DR substantially: tier multipliers 0.98/0.96/0.94/0.92 with a base mod of .16, versus S2's 0.95/0.9/0.85/0.8 with a base mod of .017. Each step reduces the new value by the next tier.
nodes.norm_label: s3 vs s2 diminishing returns tiers

nodes.label: Sqrt Scaling (AoE Target-Count Falloff)
nodes.rationale: AoE abilities deal full damage up to a per-ability TargetCountThreshold; above it each target takes base_damage * sqrt(threshold / N). Elarion Multishot threshold is 12, from AC_Hero_Bowguy.csv Bowguy.AoeProjectileDamage.TargetCountThreshold.

nodes.label: Spirit Generation Formula
nodes.rationale: spirit = enemy.SpiritPointValue * min(dmg, enemyMaxHP)/enemyMaxHP * Hero.SpiritPointGain.SpiritPointsFromDamageScaler. Mobs carry a spirit pool (void lord = 400) split across the group over time by damage dealt.

nodes.label: Armor and Magic Damage Reduction
nodes.rationale: Armor DR = (armor * 0.0052) / (7 + armor * 0.0048); magic DR sources multiply as (1 - a) * (1 - b) with total DR = 1 - result.

nodes.label: Focus Regeneration
nodes.rationale: Base 5 focus per second, scaled by haste as 5 * (1 + haste%).

nodes.label: Crit Damage and Crit Mod Math
nodes.rationale: Expected damage = (base_dmg * non_crit_chance) + (base_dmg * crit_chance * crit_dmg_mod); crit damage mods combine as 2 * (1 + mod + mod + mod). Elarion purple 30% crit and last light 30% factor in as crit_pct + .3 * .8.
nodes.norm_label: crit damage and crit mod math

nodes.label: Hero Name Mapping (dev name -> display name)
nodes.rationale: FSL class dev names differ from in-game hero names: Bowguy=Elarion, Firemage=Ardeos, Ink=Tariq, Lisa=Aeona, Mosse=Sylvie, Sune=Xavian, Vigor=Vigour, Warmaster=Helena; Gunde, Mara, Meiko, Rime match. Sourced from script_libs/fs_constants.py.
nodes.norm_label: hero name mapping (dev name -> display name)

nodes.label: Hero Roles
nodes.rationale: Three healers (Aeona, Sylvie, Vigour), three tanks (Helena, Meiko, Xavian), three ranged DPS (Ardeos, Elarion, Rime), three melee DPS (Gunde, Mara, Tariq).

nodes.label: Hero Resource Types
nodes.rationale: Per-hero list of resource type IDs where the first entry is the spendable resource; e.g. Rime uses [2 Primary, 4 Spirit, 5 Secondary] and Sylvie uses [1 Mana, 4 Spirit, 5 Secondary]. Every hero carries 4 (Spirit).

nodes.label: Resource Type ID List
nodes.rationale: 1 Mana, 2 Primary, 3 Toughness, 4 Spirit, 5 Secondary, 7 Stagger. Gunde's resource 2 is displayed in-game as 'Feathers' while all other heroes call it 'Primary'.

nodes.label: Zone Name Mapping
nodes.rationale: Dev folder -> [display name, FSL encounter id, FSL zone id, status, zone_type]. zone_type distinguishes adventure, capstone, pinnacle, and practice; status marks dead zones present in files but not live. MoorCastle, SandTomb, and SnowPeak still have TBD FSL ids pending launch logs.

nodes.label: Zone Dev Prefix to Folder
nodes.rationale: Two-letter mob dev-name prefixes identify the owning zone; note BM maps to SandTomb rather than a matching initialism.

nodes.label: Zone Short Names
nodes.rationale: Folder name to short label used in FoundInZones tracking; covers only live zones.

nodes.label: Weapon Name Mapping
nodes.rationale: Dev ability class -> in-game weapon display name, sourced from FSL/game files rather than fs_constants. Includes ChanneledCooldownReducer = Chronoshift and InstantDamageAccumulativeDebuff = Voidbringer's Touch.

nodes.label: Weapon Trait Name Mapping
nodes.rationale: Dev class -> trait display name; the behavior is encoded in the dev class name (e.g. WeaponAndSpiritPoints = Visions of Grandeur, WeaponCritChanceCooldownReduction = Brave Machinations). Two cooldown-recovery trait classes were removed.

nodes.label: Affix Mapping
nodes.rationale: Dungeon affix dev class -> in-game display name; Carnage was removed in S3 and DispelAndInterrupt / NoDispelNoInterrupt both display as Elheryn's Exile. S3 new affix dev names are still unconfirmed pending launch logs.

nodes.label: Hero Ultimate FSL Spell IDs
nodes.rationale: FSL spell id per hero ultimate. Ardeos (1001270) is flagged as not tracking properly in FSL, and Gunde's id is unknown until S3 launch logs land.

nodes.label: Splash Loading Screen (fa-splash)
nodes.rationale: Static pre-Blazor markup inside #app: brand, tagline, an ARIA progressbar (#fa-splash-bar with #fa-splash-bar-fill), and a status line driven by js/splash.js. splash.css is preloaded so the first paint is not blocked on the runtime download.

nodes.label: Manual Blazor WebAssembly Bootstrap
nodes.rationale: blazor.webassembly.js is loaded with autostart="false" so js/splash.js can drive startup and report download/runtime progress into the splash bar before handing control to the client app.

nodes.label: External Font and Icon CDN Assets
nodes.rationale: Nunito and Noto Sans from Google Fonts (with preconnect hints) and Tabler Icons webfont 3.45.0 from jsDelivr are fetched off-CDN rather than bundled, keeping them out of the AOT-compiled WASM payload.
nodes.norm_label: external font and icon cdn assets

nodes.label: Armor Damage Reduction Curve (S2) chart
nodes.rationale: Dark-themed line plot (gold curve on navy) titled 'Armor Damage Reduction Curve (S2)': x-axis Armor 0-1500, y-axis Damage Reduction (%) 0-60. The formula is printed in monospace in the lower right of the plot area and five armor values are annotated with arrows. Published as a reference figure so the Season 2 armor mitigation curve can be reproduced exactly rather than guessed from in-game observation.

nodes.label: Armor damage reduction formula: (armor x 0.0052) / (7 + armor x 0.0048)
nodes.rationale: Printed verbatim on the chart as `(armor x 0.0052) / (7 + armor x 0.0048)`. Result is a fraction (multiply by 100 for the plotted percentage): armor=100 gives 0.52/7.48 = 0.0695 = 7.0%, armor=1200 gives 6.24/12.76 = 0.489 = 48.9%, both matching the annotated points. A rational (Michaelis-Menten style) form is chosen over a linear one so each additional point of armor is worth strictly less than the last, keeping stacking armor useful but never dominant.
nodes.norm_label: armor damage reduction formula: (armor x 0.0052) / (7 + armor x 0.0048)

nodes.label: Armor (input stat)
nodes.rationale: The only free variable in the formula and the chart's x-axis. Plotted range 0-1500 implies that is the practically relevant armor band for Season 2 characters.

nodes.label: Damage reduction (%) output
nodes.rationale: The chart's y-axis and the formula's result: the fraction of incoming damage mitigated by armor. Over the plotted band it spans 0% to roughly 55%.

nodes.label: Diminishing returns on armor stacking
nodes.rationale: The concave shape is the whole point of the figure. Marginal value per point of armor falls steadily: the first 100 armor buys 7.0% mitigation, while the 400 armor from 800 to 1200 buys only a further 10.5%. Because armor appears in both numerator and denominator, the curve saturates instead of running away, so no amount of armor can trivialise incoming damage.

nodes.label: Numerator coefficient 0.0052
nodes.rationale: Scales raw armor into mitigation units; together with the denominator constant it sets the near-linear early slope (approximately 0.0052/7 = 0.074% mitigation per point of armor at low armor).

nodes.label: Denominator coefficient 0.0048
nodes.rationale: The self-scaling term that produces the saturation: armor feeds back into its own denominator, so the ratio of the two coefficients (0.0052/0.0048) fixes the curve's ceiling.

nodes.label: Denominator constant 7
nodes.rationale: Acts as the half-value scale constant: mitigation reaches half its asymptote when armor x 0.0048 equals 7, i.e. around 1458 armor. Larger values of this constant would flatten the whole curve.

nodes.label: Asymptotic mitigation ceiling (~108%, unreachable in the plotted band)
nodes.rationale: As armor grows without bound the formula tends to 0.0052/0.0048 = 1.083, i.e. 108%, which is above full immunity. The plotted 0-1500 armor band tops out near 55%, so the mathematical ceiling is never approached in practice; whether the game applies a separate hard cap is not shown on the figure.
nodes.norm_label: asymptotic mitigation ceiling (~108%, unreachable in the plotted band)

nodes.label: Annotated armor breakpoints (100/300/500/800/1200)
nodes.rationale: Five arrow-annotated reference points on the curve: 100 -> 7.0%, 300 -> 18.5%, 500 -> 27.7%, 800 -> 38.4%, 1200 -> 48.9%. They double as a verification table for any reimplementation of the formula.

nodes.label: Season 2 (S2) armor tuning
nodes.rationale: The '(S2)' in the title scopes the constants to Season 2 game data, so the coefficients are season-versioned and must be re-derived rather than assumed stable across seasons.
